canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing is assigning a class or category label to an input or whole image from a predefined set. A recurrent usage, especially with vision-language models, casts this as zero-shot or prompt-based prediction by comparing images with text prompts or class descriptions; in Understanding prompt engineering may not require rethinking generalization, the task is described as "image classification via pretrained vision-language models" with prompts chosen to maximize training accuracy without finetuning. Many other papers use supervised fine-tuning or in-context classification from labeled image-label examples, and Context is Environment extends the goal to obtaining a predictor that can "correctly classify x in new cities" under environment shift.

Variants. Papers also carve out narrower forms of the behavior, most often zero-shot or few-shot classification, including in-context setups where labeled examples appear in the prompt. Others shift the scope from whole-image labels to object-level categorization, sometimes on cropped objects with the category produced through natural language generation. Domain-specific versions include species classification, cell type classification, and industrial product classification, and some papers group these tasks under broader labels such as visual classification or image recognition.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers operationalize it with 26 linked measurement instruments. The most frequent are ImageNet-1k, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, VTAB-1k, and Food-101. These instruments are mostly benchmark datasets or benchmark suites for image classification, and papers use them in zero-shot, fine-tuning, transfer, and adaptation evaluations; VTAB-1k is described as a suite of 19 diverse visual classification tasks.

What it is taken as evidence of. Only a mixed set of 6 constructs is linked to this behavior, and the links point in several directions rather than a single shared framing. One paper uses image classification to measure Generalization. Separate papers claim a causal relationship from Image classification to General ability, and from Multimodal alignment and Fine-grained perception to Image classification; other papers report that Image classification is related to In-context learning and to Visual understanding.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing is assigning a class or category label to an input or whole image from a predefined set. A recurrent usage, especially with vision-language models, casts this as zero-shot or prompt-based prediction by comparing images with text prompts or class descriptions; in Understanding prompt engineering may not require rethinking generalization, the task is described as "image classification via pretrained vision-language models" with prompts chosen to maximize training accuracy without finetuning. Many other papers use supervised fine-tuning or in-context classification from labeled image-label examples, and Context is Environment extends the goal to obtaining a predictor that can "correctly classify x in new cities" under environment shift.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: Papers also carve out narrower forms of the behavior, most often zero-shot or few-shot classification, including in-context setups where labeled examples appear in the prompt. Others shift the scope from whole-image labels to object-level categorization, sometimes on cropped objects with the category produced through natural language generation. Domain-specific versions include species classification, cell type classification, and industrial product classification, and some papers group these tasks under broader labels such as visual classification or image recognition.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers operationalize it with 26 linked measurement instruments. The most frequent are ImageNet-1k, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, VTAB-1k, and Food-101. These instruments are mostly benchmark datasets or benchmark suites for image classification, and papers use them in zero-shot, fine-tuning, transfer, and adaptation evaluations; VTAB-1k is described as a suite of 19 diverse visual classification tasks.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Only a mixed set of 6 constructs is linked to this behavior, and the links point in several directions rather than a single shared framing. One paper uses image classification to measure Generalization. Separate papers claim a causal relationship from Image classification to General ability, and from Multimodal alignment and Fine-grained perception to Image classification; other papers report that Image classification is related to In-context learning and to Visual understanding.
